relatedSnapshot.title: Lead import blocked in free workspaces: Add Leads Confirm stays disabled when the workspace lead-capacity lookup fails
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>
Contact: Name 1 (<email>), owner of the "Company One" client workspace (free workspace, Company Two subworkspace "Company One").

## Bounded conversation context

The same open Intercom conversation first asked how many free workspaces the plan includes (support answered 4 and added them), then, on 2026-09-30/10-01, reported: "I'm having trouble in a new client's workspace. The workspace is titled Company One. There are two Company Eight and I am talking about the active one. When I research leads in acquisity and build a lead list and then go to the next screen, I am unable to import leads even though I have 12,000 lead credits." Follow-ups: "I'm unable to click 'confirm' once i enter any number of leads. This is preventing me from moving forward with the campaign." Support asked whether another browser helped; the customer replied yes, and attached a second screenshot: "Same issue". Two screenshots attached (error.png, Screenshot 2026-10-02 100120.png).

## Testable claim

In a free workspace, the "Add Leads To Campaign" dialog leaves the Confirm button permanently disabled for every lead count, because the workspace lead-capacity lookup (integrations.Company Two.getWorkspacePlanDetails) fails with PRECONDITION_FAILED ("We could not safely verify the organization-wide Growth lead capacity, so this ingestion was not started."), and the UI treats missing plan details as "cannot import" without showing any reason.

## Observed symptom (both screenshots read)

* Name 2 "Add Leads To Campaign": Estimated available leads 10,683 and 5,259; "12,500 lead credits remaining" badge (green); entered counts 1000 and 200; Confirm greyed out/disabled; no validation or error message anywhere in the dialog.
* The dialog shows no workspace capacity card and no explanation, so the customer had no way to know why the button was disabled.

## Evidence

* Sentry ACQUISITY-4XX, event 2026-10-06T07:58:27Z, user <email>, tag procedure=integrations.Company Two.getWorkspacePlanDetails, procedureType=query, trpcErrorCode=PRECONDITION_FAILED, release 25bb06339fe20b9eff481280e5b88eafe09818a2. Issue unresolved/ongoing: 3,012 occurrences, 813 users impacted since 2026-09-04.
* Production: the workspace is a free workspace (free_workspace row) whose Autumn billing account carries only credit packs (2,500 + 10,000 credits, 12,500 remaining, 0 used) and domain/inbox add-ons, with no base-plan subscription, so the capacity plan classification resolves to unresolved_autumn.
* No lead_scrape_run and no lead-search submission exists for the workspace: the blocked action never reached the server, which matches a client-side disabled button.

## Code path

* apps/web/trpc/routers/integrations/Company Two.ts -> getWorkspacePlanDetails: throws growthLeadCapacityUnavailableError when resolveOrganizationLeadCapacityProjection returns 'unresolved_autumn'.
* apps/web/lib/outreach/capacity/plan-classification.ts -> classifyOrganizationLeadCapacityPlan: returns 'unresolved_autumn' when the Autumn account has no base plan in the catalog.
* apps/web/hooks/campaign/use-workspace-lead-limits.ts -> canImportLeads: returns false whenever planDetails is missing, so every count fails.
* apps/web/components/campaigns/new/steps/add-leads-dialog.tsx -> canConfirm / Confirm button: workspaceCanFit false disables Confirm with no message.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-10-06)

* PlanetScale: 667 active free workspaces; 301 of them have an active outreach provider.
* Sentry ACQUISITY-4XX: 813 users impacted, 3,012 events, still occurring.

relatedSnapshot.title: Campaign launch returns a generic error because the workspace's own Company Two connection is rejected
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: On 2026-09-24 the customer in "Name 5's Workspace" reported that trying to launch a campaign gives "Something went wrong", and linked the campaign "Name 6 | Marketing agencies | US | Leadership | AIA Created\*". Support asked for the campaign name and the customer has not replied yet.

Finding: the launch fails because the workspace's own Company Two connection is being rejected by Company Two, not because of anything in the campaign setup.

* Launch attempt on this campaign on 2026-09-24 20:39 UTC failed with a generic internal error (Sentry ACQUISITY-4RB, outreach.campaigns.resumeCampaign, campaign and organization match).
* The same provider answered Company Two API Client Error (402) "Workspace does not have an active paid plan" from the email-accounts screen at 23:12 UTC (Sentry ACQUISITY-2ZE), and a connection test at 23:12 UTC stored "The request was rejected by Company Two. Please verify your API key." on the provider record.
* This is a legacy direct connection to the customer's own Company Two account (account_type user_owned, connected by the workspace owner on 2026-05-08). The Company Two plan, billing and API key live inside that account.
* Campaign setup is intact: status draft, never launched, 2,496 of 2,500 leads were pushed to Company Two on 2026-09-17. The workspace has sent almost nothing since 2026-09-17.

What a person should do: Support should tell the customer the campaign name is known and that the blocker is their Company Two connection. Walk them through Settings, Cold Email Agent, Outreach Providers (visible to owners and admins): run Test Connection, read the error, and confirm the Company Two account that holds this workspace is on an active paid plan with a current API key. Reconnecting with a fresh Company Two key is the customer-side action. Acquisity cannot see or change plan state inside Company Two, and support has the same limit.

No engineering work was created: the campaign is fine and the provider is rejecting the connection. The generic error message on launch is a known product gap, tracked by ENG-13812.

Reopen if: a connection test passes for this workspace and the launch still fails, which would move the cause back into the launch path.

relatedSnapshot.title: Campaigns launched with no leads get stuck in 'completed' status permanently
relatedSnapshot.description:
*Important to get this fixed quickly as campaigns are set to auto launch by default - if there is no leads by the time it's created they get stuck in this cycle. The only fix is to download the leads, delete the leads, and then duplicate the campaign and re-upload.*

## Bug Report

When an email campaign is launched with no leads uploaded yet, it transitions to **completed** status. Once leads are subsequently uploaded, the campaign remains stuck in **completed** and does not resume sending.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create and launch an email campaign with **no leads uploaded**
2. The campaign transitions to `completed` status (because Company Two marks it as completed when there are no leads to send to)
3. Upload leads to the campaign
4. Campaign remains stuck in `completed` status — leads are never sent
5. User can manually resume the campaign → status changes to `active`
6. After 1-2 minutes, the campaign reverts back to `completed` again despite having leads

### Root Cause Analysis (Preliminary)

The issue appears to involve two interacting problems:

1. **Company Two marks campaigns as completed (status 3) when launched with no leads.** This is expected Company Two behavior — if there are no leads, the campaign has "nothing to do" so it completes immediately.
2. **Periodic sync overwrites local status with Company Two's status.** The `syncCampaignData` Inngest function (`campaign-sync.ts`) and `campaign-import.ts` both call `mapInstantlyStatusToOur()` which maps Company Two status `3` → `OutreachCampaignStatus.Completed`. This sync runs periodically and overwrites any local status changes.
3. **Resume only updates locally, not durably against sync.** When a user resumes, the app calls Company Two's `/campaigns/{id}/activate` endpoint, which sets the campaign to active on Company Two. However, if Company Two transitions the campaign back to completed quickly (because it already processed and found no *new* unsent leads, or some race condition), the next sync cycle picks up `completed` again and overwrites the local `active` status.

### Key Files

* `lib/inngest/functions/campaign/util.ts` — `mapInstantlyStatusToOur()` (line 142)
* `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/campaign-sync.ts` — status sync logic (line 304)
* `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/campaign-import.ts` — import status mapping (line 323)
* `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/periodic-sync.ts` — periodic sync trigger
* `trpc/routers/outreach/campaigns.ts` — resume campaign endpoint (line 1889)

### Suggested Fix

The sync process should not overwrite a campaign's status to `completed` if the campaign has been resumed or has pending/unsent leads. Consider:

* Adding a guard in the sync that checks for uploaded leads before allowing transition to `completed`
* Preserving user-initiated status changes (e.g. resume) by skipping provider status sync for recently-resumed campaigns
* Not mapping Company Two's `completed` status when the campaign has leads that haven't been contacted yet

relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox

relatedSnapshot.title: Managed-workspace setup rebinds the Company Two provider before its later steps can fail, leaving the workspace unable to launch campaigns
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Moving a workspace onto Acquisity-managed sending can fail after the workspace's Company Two provider has already been rebound to the newly created managed sub-workspace. The workspace is then left pointing at a workspace that holds none of its campaigns or inboxes, so campaign launch and resume fail with a generic error and the customer has no way back.

## Problem

An owner follows the product's own route to managed sending (Settings > Cold Email Agent > Edit under Outreach Provider). The workspace setup run creates the managed sub-workspace and rebinds the provider, then dies at a later step. From then on every campaign launch and resume in that workspace returns "Something went wrong". The email-accounts screen shows no inboxes, and nothing tells the customer or support that the workspace is half-migrated.

## Root cause

apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-workspace-setup.ts performs the irreversible rebind at the update-provider-workspace-id step (\~557-629), which for a user-owned source calls createProvider (apps/web/lib/services/outreach-provider.ts \~1037-1061): it updates the existing Company Two provider row in place, replaces its credentials with the agency key and workspace suffix, and sets account_type=system_provisioned with skip_workspace_id_check=false. Later steps can still fail and there is no rollback: revoke-source-provider-webhook (\~712) aborts the run on an Company Two error (observed: 402 "Workspace does not have an active paid plan" from the legacy account being retired), so clear-source-provider-snapshot (\~767), trigger-campaign-sync (\~788) and the workspace billing step never run. The launch path (apps/web/lib/services/campaign-launcher.ts launchOrResumeCampaign \~182) then resolves the campaign through the rebound provider and its Company Two workspace scoping (apps/web/lib/outreach/Company Two/client.ts request \~513), does not find the campaign in the empty managed sub-workspace, and resumeCampaign (apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/campaigns.ts \~6398) reports the thrown error as the generic "Failed to resume campaign".

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected: 2 orgs and 2 users in the last 30 days, counted 2026-09-25 from production submission:
select count(distinct organization_id) as orgs, count(\*) from submission where type='workspace_create' and status='failed' and created_at > now() - interval '30 days' and metadata->>'diagnosticError' like 'Company Two API Client Error (402)%'  -> 2 orgs. One workspace remains unable to launch any campaign; the state of the other after its failure was not inspected.
Path context from the same window: 5 workspace_create submissions reached the managed-inbox migration step (3 completed, 2 failed); 308 submissions in total, 3 failed. Limitation: the recorded skip reason does not separate a legacy user-owned source from an icemail source.

## Proposed fix

The setup must be atomic in effect. If any step after the provider rebind fails, the workspace must be returned to a working provider binding (the pre-rebind snapshot in submission.result.sourceProviderSnapshot exists for exactly this) or the run must be resumable to completion, and the workspace must never rest in a state where its provider points at a sub-workspace that does not hold its campaigns and inboxes. In that state, launch and resume must surface the real reason instead of the generic error.

## What's included

Decided scope: rebind-or-rollback semantics in process-workspace-setup.ts, and a launch/resume failure that names the workspace state. Excluded: the generic launch error message itself, already tracked by ENG-13812. Depends on: the legacy-account webhook revocation being allowed to fail without aborting the run. Separately deliverable: customer recovery for the affected workspace, and an alert when a setup run fails after the rebind.

## Regression seam

Trigger: a workspace_create for an org whose active provider is a legacy user-owned Company Two connection, with the source-provider webhook revocation forced to fail. Red before: the provider row ends system_provisioned bound to a sub-workspace with no campaigns while the run is failed, and a subsequent campaign resume throws. Green after: either the run completes and the campaign resumes, or the provider binding is restored and resume no longer throws, with the submission recording which.

## Done when

* A workspace_create run that fails after update-provider-workspace-id leaves the workspace in a provider state that can launch its campaigns, or is explicitly marked as needing completion.
* A campaign launch or resume in a workspace whose provider points at a workspace without that campaign returns a specific, actionable error instead of the generic failure.
* A regression test at the workspace-setup seam proves the red-before / green-after behavior above.

## Reports

* ENG-14269

relatedSnapshot.title: Free workspaces cannot import leads: workspace lead capacity never resolves, so Add Leads Confirm stays disabled
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Free workspaces billed through Autumn cannot import leads at all. The Add Leads to Campaign dialog's Confirm button stays disabled for every lead count, with no message explaining why, so customers who bought lead credits on such a workspace cannot spend them.

## Problem

An owner of a free workspace runs an AI lead search, opens Add Leads to Campaign, types any number of leads, and Confirm never enables. Nothing on the screen says why, and the workspace has ample lead credits and ample search results. The same block hits every count, in any browser.

## Root cause

The workspace's campaign-lead capacity cannot be resolved, and the UI reads "no capacity answer" as "cannot import".

* apps/web/trpc/routers/integrations/Company Two.ts -> getWorkspacePlanDetails throws growthLeadCapacityUnavailableError (TRPCError PRECONDITION_FAILED, "We could not safely verify the organization-wide Growth lead capacity, so this ingestion was not started.") when resolveOrganizationLeadCapacityProjection answers 'unresolved_autumn'.
* apps/web/lib/outreach/capacity/plan-classification.ts -> classifyOrganizationLeadCapacityPlan answers 'unresolved_autumn' when the Autumn billing account has no base plan in the catalog, because resolveStrictAutumnPlan returns null. A free workspace gets its own billing account holding only credit packs and domain/inbox add-ons, so it lands here.
* apps/web/hooks/campaign/use-workspace-lead-limits.ts -> canImportLeads returns false whenever planDetails is missing, and apps/web/components/campaigns/new/steps/add-leads-dialog.tsx -> canConfirm makes the Confirm button depend on it.
* apps/web/components/campaigns/instantly-lead-limit-card.tsx hides itself when (error || !planDetails), so the one card that could explain a capacity problem never renders in this case.

Introduced by ENG-13131 "Enforce Growth's organization-wide 5,000-lead capacity" (parent ENG-13107 "Add $99/month plan with reduced lead limit", completed 2026-08-28), which built the Growth organization-wide capacity rule and the reservation machinery, promised that Pro and partner behaviour stayed unchanged, and made no decision for Base/free workspaces. Sentry first-seen 2026-09-04 is consistent with that date.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-10-06.

* Confirmed affected: 1 workspace with direct evidence (the reporting workspace), which has an active campaign provider and a purchase of lead credits it cannot spend.
* Potentially exposed: 255 Autumn-billed free workspaces with an active outreach provider, out of 491 Autumn-billed free workspaces. Query: select count(distinct fw.organization_id) as free_ws_all, count(distinct case when op.id is not null then fw.organization_id end) as free_ws_with_provider, count(distinct case when ba.provider = 'autumn' then fw.organization_id end) as autumn_free_ws, count(distinct case when ba.provider = 'autumn' and op.id is not null then fw.organization_id end) as autumn_free_with_provider from free_workspace fw join organization o on o.id = fw.organization_id join billing_account ba on ba.id = o.billing_account_id left join outreach_provider op on op.organization_id = fw.organization_id and op.is_active = true where o.deleted_at is null; returned 667 / 301 / 491 / 255. Partner-billed free workspaces (176, of which 46 have an active provider) are excluded because plan-classification.ts lines 92-94 answer 'known_non_growth' for a non-Autumn provider before any Autumn read, so they never reach the throw.
* Upper bound from runtime telemetry, not a filtered count: the error's Sentry issue shows 813 users impacted and 3,012 events since 2026-09-04, still occurring; that issue groups by error message and its events carry other procedures and impersonated support sessions.
* What blocks an exact figure: no telemetry currently counts blocked imports or unresolvable capacity per workspace.

## Proposed fix

Make the capacity resolution answer for an Autumn-billed free workspace instead of throwing: give the classification a defined outcome for a workspace with no base plan, so the plan-details query returns a capacity rather than a PRECONDITION_FAILED error. In the same pass, make the dialog tell the user why Confirm is disabled whenever the capacity answer is missing, and cover the provider-402 null case as well, where a system-provisioned workspace with no active paid provider plan also returns null and silently disables Confirm through the same helper.

## What's included

* The classification outcome for a free workspace and the capacity answer it produces.
* A user-visible reason for a disabled Confirm, for both the thrown error and the null response.
* Telemetry that counts blocked imports and unresolvable capacity per workspace.
* Excluded: any change to the Growth 5,000-lead rule itself, and any data repair for affected customers, because nothing was written and no credits were spent.
* Dependency: the capacity classification and its Autumn base-plan catalog resolution.

## Regression seam

plan-classification.ts classifyOrganizationLeadCapacityPlan, extending the existing "treats missing or ambiguous Autumn identity as unresolved" case with a free-workspace case, plus a free-workspace case in the integrations.Company Two router test where getWorkspacePlanDetails must return a capacity instead of throwing. Red before: the query throws PRECONDITION_FAILED and Confirm stays disabled for a valid count. Green after: the query returns a capacity and Confirm enables.

## Done when

* A free workspace with no base plan resolves a campaign-lead capacity and can import leads.
* The Add Leads dialog shows a reason whenever capacity disables Confirm.
* A regression test proves the free-workspace case at the named seam.
* Blocked imports and unresolvable capacity are countable per workspace.

## Reports

* ENG-14774 Lead import blocked in free workspaces: Add Leads Confirm stays disabled when the workspace lead-capacity lookup fails
